content: Indication-specific dosing for glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) and liver extract glandular products in combination should be carefully followed based on product labeling and titrated as indicated. The recommended daily dose for spleen peptides is 5 grams, which includes 50 mg of tuftsin and splenopentin. Alternatively, 120 mg of pure polypeptides or 750 mg of crude polypeptide fractions can be administered daily. Dosage varies depending on the specific product. These products are used for various indications, including vascular insufficiencies, as adjunctive therapy in hepatic disorders, as a source of heme iron, for allergies, chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS), enhancing muscle development in bodybuilders, and improving strength and stamina. They may also serve as digestive aids when taken with food, exhibit anti-inflammatory properties, and be used in conditions such as herpes zoster and immune complex diseases. Post-splenectomy, these products are indicated for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), AIDS, colitis, rheumatoid arthritis (RA), low white blood cell (WBC) count, thrombocytopenia, ulcerative colitis, and enhancing immune function in cancer patients. They are also used for immune system modulation in upper respiratory infections (URI), hepatitis B, AIDS, allergies, cancer, rheumatoid arthritis, chronic fatigue syndrome, lupus, and for increasing WBC production in cancer patients undergoing radiation or chemotherapy. Additionally, they may have applications in addressing aging-related immune decline. For hypothyroidism, the effectiveness of these products depends on the extraction method, with predigested soluble concentrates generally being the most effective. Physiological studies have demonstrated gastrointestinal absorption of intact macromolecules, such as polypeptides, and human trials have shown efficacy for the listed uses. However, thyroid extracts are more challenging to calibrate compared to synthetic hormones. Glandular products have been shown to increase the effects of levothyroxine, liothyronine, and thyroid desiccated products through pharmacodynamic synergism. These effects are considered minor, and their clinical significance remains unknown. Additive effects may occur when used with thyroid glandular extracts. Adverse effects include allergic reactions, infections, or other symptoms due to contaminants, though these are rare. Liver extract products may lead to iron overload or hemochromatosis, while thyroid extracts can cause hyperthyroid symptoms when taken in large doses. Hypersensitivity to bovine or porcine products is also a potential concern. These extracts are typically derived from whole glandular tissue of bovine or porcine origin. Regarding pregnancy and lactation, there is no specific category assigned (N/A). However, these products are generally considered acceptable, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
